title: I saw a game on Steam Next Fest that wasn't release yet, so I built it myself
author: beelllllll
selftext:
I saw a game on the Steam Next Fest that hit all my favorite notes: grid tactics, autobattler flow, and really tactical combat.

I didn’t feel like waiting months (maybe years?) for it to release, so I spun up my Claude Code + AutoSprite agentic workflow and built a prototype of my own take on it (obviously with final fantasy tactics inspired epic summons and limit breaks).

Curious if people are into this type of game.   
  
I'm happy to share more about how I made it, my workflow, or anything else.

Happy to hear any early feedback too!

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body: That looks awesome! Not an autobattler fan myself but it looks great. What's the workflow?

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body:
Thanks! I have really been perfecting my process, but currently here is how I do it:

First: I make a full product requirements document with claude or chatgpt (this takes the most human brain power time) I spend like at least an hour or two on it. It has a deep description of every screen, every character, every ability, every cooldown, all the assets we will need, animations. It has a huge section on typical battle flow. I even make ascii diagrams of the screens (you can even upload like hand drawn sketches). This is just a massive text document.

  
Second:  
I download the prd text document and put it into an empty directory on my computer. I open Claude Code (I use terminal but you can use Cursor or the claude app or any agent really) and I literally say 'implement this prd end to end'. It crunches for like an hour. This gets you 80% of the way there, you have a functional game with placeholder graphics.

Third:   
I got to [https://www.autosprite.io/](https://www.autosprite.io/) (it's my product full disclosure) and I create all the characters and assets and animations I'll need. At this point you can just download them to the game folder and tell claude to add them to the game, but I go one step further and have claude connect to the AutoSprite MCP server, and claude automatically finds all the characters and downloads them (I can go more into detail on this if you want, but it's an optional step that just makes it easier and faster)

After that its just adding polish, balancing, and completing the full gameplay loop.
